---
title: "check-r-head.yml"
---

Diff-scoped check that flags an R statement
printing a dataset through `head()` in a data div,
such as `head(df)` or `df |> head()`.
Where a page shows a dataset,
its R chunk prints the data frame itself,
and the format's `df-print` decides how much each reader sees:
`paged` on the website and in the slide decks,
and `tibble` in the PDF handouts
([#2122](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/issues/2122)).
Elsewhere, `head()` is fine.

## Where it applies

The check reads, in `.qmd`, `.Rmd`, and `.md` files:

- every `{r}` chunk of a data subfile,
  a file whose base name matches `data-files`
  (default `_dat-*`, such as `_dat-auto.qmd` or `_dat-auto-preview.qmd`);
- every `{r}` chunk inside a fenced div whose id starts `#dat-`,
  in any file.

## What it flags

A top-level R statement whose printed value comes from `head()`:

- a call: `head(df)` or `utils::head(df, 3)`;
- a pipeline whose last stage is `head`,
  as in `df |> head()`, `df %>% head(n = 3)`, or `df %>% head`;
- the same wrapped in `print()`,
  as in `print(head(df))` or `df |> head() |> print()`.

A statement can span lines
while a bracket is open or a line ends in an operator,
and the finding names the line that holds `head`.

The check does not flag:

- an R chunk outside a data subfile or a `#dat-` div;
- an assignment: `top <- head(df)` or `df |> head() -> top`;
- `head()` passed to another call (`nrow(head(df))`)
  or followed by another pipeline stage (`df |> head() |> knitr::kable()`);
- a statement inside braces, such as a function body or a loop;
- a method or field, such as `df.head()`, `x$head()`, or `slice_head()`;
- `head` inside an R comment or a string;
- a chunk in another engine (`{python}`, `{julia}`),
  a plain `r` fence, an escaped `{{r}}` chunk,
  or a chunk shown inside a longer fence;
- a statement carrying, or following,
  `# check-r-head: allow: <reason>`.
  The reason is required.

## Scope

Only statements with a line a pull request adds are reported,
so existing pages never block.
An added line whose exact text was also deleted in the same diff
counts as moved rather than new.

With no `base-ref`, or when the diff cannot be computed
(a shallow clone, an unresolvable ref),
the check skips with a warning.
It never falls back to a whole-tree scan.
Set `whole-tree: true` to scan every tracked file in full on purpose.

Every run prints how many lines and files it examined.

## Limitations

- A string that spans lines can hide or invent a `head`.
- A data div written as an `include` of a file the patterns do not match
  is read only through the including page's own `#dat-` div,
  not through the included file.
- A brand new untracked file is invisible to `git diff`.
  Stage it to have a local run examine it.

## Inputs

| Input            | Type    | Default | Description |
| ---------------- | ------- | ------- | ----------- |
| `data-files`     | string  | `'_dat-*'` | Space- or comma-separated file-name patterns, matched against a file's base name, of data subfiles whose every R chunk is checked. |
| `globs`          | string  | `'*.qmd *.Rmd *.md'` | Space-separated git pathspecs of tracked files to check (recursive by default). |
| `paths-ignore`   | string  | `''`    | Comma- or newline-separated glob patterns (relative paths) to skip. Supports `*`, `?` and recursive `**`. |
| `fail`           | boolean | `true`  | Fail the workflow when a printed `head()` is found. Set `false` to warn only. |
| `whole-tree`     | boolean | `false` | Scan every tracked file in full instead of only a PR's added lines. |
| `python-version` | string  | `'3.x'` | Python version to set up. |
| `runs-on` | string | empty (`CI_RUNNER` variable, else `ubuntu-latest`) | Runner label for the job. Use a self-hosted label only for a private repository; never for a public one, whose pull requests can run arbitrary code on it ([#1167](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/issues/1167)). |

## Permissions

Only `contents: read` (the default), so no `permissions:` block is needed.

## Example

```yaml
# Copy to .github/workflows/check-r-head.yml in your repo.
# Diff-scoped check: flags an R statement that prints a dataset through head(),
# such as `head(df)` or `df |> head()`, in a data div (a `_dat-*` subfile or a
# `#dat-` div), on lines a PR adds. The chunk prints the data frame itself, and
# the format's df-print decides how much each reader sees.
# Blocks by default; existing pages never block, since only added lines count.
# Only contents:read is needed (the default), so no permissions block is required.
name: Check printed head() in data divs

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  check:
    uses: Morrison-Lab/gha/.github/workflows/check-r-head.yml@v3
    # with:
    #   data-files: '_dat-*'                    # base-name patterns of data subfiles
    #   globs: '*.qmd *.md'                     # pathspecs to check (recursive)
    #   paths-ignore: 'chapters/outtakes/**'    # skip known-noisy paths
    #   fail: false                             # warn instead of block (defaults to true)
    #   whole-tree: true                        # scan every line, not just a PR's additions
    #   runs-on: private-runner                # self-hosted runner label (private repositories only)
```

See
[`examples/check-r-head.yml`](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/blob/main/examples/check-r-head.yml)
for the full caller stub.
